newsitem.title: USA: Fred Meyer sees earnings boost.
newsitem.headline: Fred Meyer sees earnings boost.

text.p: Fred Meyer Inc said Wednesday it completed a series of property deals that will boost its annual earnings per share estimates by about $0.20 a share in 1997 and future years.

The company said in a statement that it completed a series of deals affecting the 35 store leases and its Clackamas, Oregon distribution center that it began leasing from Metropolitan Life Insurance Co in 1986. The transactions will cut annual pretax occupancy-related expenses by about $8.9 million.

Fred Meyer said it will spend $49 million to buy six stores leased from MetLife, including one store that was previously closed, plus an option to purchase 25 outparcels at 18 of the 29 stores it will continue to lease from MetLife.

The company's Clackamas distribution center will be sold by MetLife to a third party and leased to Fred Meyer at reduced rents. The company has negotiated 25-year leases from MetLife on the remaining 29 stores that will result in reduced rents for accounting purposes.
